summary: @servicetitan/anvil-icon preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-dispatch tables) and, when Bun is not present on PATH, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and invokes it against math_init.js — a 727KB heavily-obfuscated JavaScript blob (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, hex-named globals, large numeric string-reconstruction tables). math_init.js is not declared in package.json's `files` allowlist (which only lists mdi/*.svg icon assets) and bears no relationship to the package's stated icon-library purpose. Installing the package causes an alternate JavaScript runtime to be fetched and used to execute an undeclared opaque payload on the installer's machine, bypassing scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. The package name places it under the @servicetitan scope, which is inconsistent with the install-time behavior expected of a first-party icon library and suggests scope impersonation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
